title: Page addresses and the Roster rules
subtitle: 2 questions. Change only the ones you disagree with, then send.
facts: Inline links are the documented convention today. The comment in astro.config.mjs and the pre-commit href grep both expect ${import.meta.env.BASE_URL}district/1 written in the page. No ADR covers it.

questions.group: Candidate 2: page addresses and the Vote chip
questions.title: Who owns a page's address?
questions.body: Today the address is written at each link site and again in each route's filename and getStaticPaths params.

options.label: A. A small module outside src/domain/ knows how a District, Councilor and Council Document page is addressed, base path included. Links and route params both come from it.
B. VoteRecord hands each thing its site path alongside its other fields, and the page adds the base path.
C. Leave links inline and accept the grep. Candidate 2 shrinks to Q2.

questions.why: The base path is a build fact, not a Council rule, so it doesn't belong in VoteRecord. This module will be small: the gain is locality and a test, not depth. If that isn't worth a module to you, C is a fair answer.

questions.title: Which Roster rules get checked when a Roster is built?
questions.body: Tick every rule that should stop ingest and the build, with a message naming the entries.

options.label: 2. No two people, Councilors or Mayors, share a surname while both are in office. This covers the Mayor case too.
3. A Term's end is not before its start.
4. At most 3 Councilors serve a District on any date.
5. At most one Mayor is in office on any date.

questions.why: Rule 2 means two real Councilors with the same surname would stop ingest and the build until someone decides how the city's vote list tells them apart. That matches the Roster's existing "forced rather than guessed" rule.
